say.text: Tikrit, on the Tigris. The month of Rabi' II, 526 AH: March, 1132.
Near this fortress the armies of Zengi, lord of Mosul, and of the Seljuk prince Mas'ud have been routed by Qaraja as-Saqi, who came to the aid of the Caliph al-Mustarshid.
What is left of Zengi's host is falling back toward the river.
Ayyub keeps the citadel of Tikrit for Bihruz, the Seljuk governor of Iraq, as his father Shadi kept it before him. His brother Shirkuh serves beside him.
Look at the river road, Shirkuh. That is no army. Those are men walking home with their wounds.
Qaraja's riders cannot be far behind them. They will not stop at our gate.
No. But Zengi is somewhere in that crowd, with the water at his back.
Bihruz will have his own view of who may pass through this gate, brother. Think before you open it.
A man with nothing left in his hands is a guest at my door, whoever sent him there.
